results.title: 2015 INDOT Traffic Data
results.description:
Indiana Annual Average Daily Traffic Counts created as an ESRI Polyline Feature Class. The data set was compiled by Road Inventory and Traffic Statistics sections of the Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT) . Dataset is classified as sde Feature Class. The Feature Class is projected Coordinate System: NAD 1983, UTM, Zone 16 N. The Projections is Transverse Mercator.

AADT – Annual Average Daily Traffic. The number of vehicles estimated to travel on a segment of roadway on an average day. This value includes all vehicle classes. In most cases, it is derived from data collected over a period of 48 hours to which factors are applied to account for the day of the week and month of the year. When vehicle classification is not collected, a factor to adjust for the excess vehicles caused by multi-axle trucks is applied. For locations where data was not collected in the current year, an Annual Growth factor is applied to the most recent data to estimate a current year value. The factors are developed from data collected at Continuous Collection sites across the State on a variety of road types.

AADT_SU –  Annual Average Daily Traffic of Single-Unit Vehicles. The number of vehicles from the AADT that are classified according to FHWA Scheme F as 4, 5, 6, or 7. Such vehicles are characterized by two or more axles on a single frame. Some common vehicles included here are Buses, Box Trucks, Large Ambulances, and Dump Trucks.

AADT_COMBO – Annual Average Daily Traffic of Combination Unit Vehicles. The number of vehicles from the AADT that are classified according to FHWA Scheme F as 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, or 13. Such vehicles are characterized as having two or more units consisting of a Tractor with two or more axles pulling one or more Trailers. The most common of these is the 18 wheel semi-truck.

results.title: Indianapolis MPO Traffic Analysis Zone Boundaries
results.description:
Overview

This Feature Service provides detailed polygon boundaries for Traffic Analysis Zones (TAZ) used by the Indianapolis Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) for travel demand modeling as of the year 2026. The data represents spatial divisions within the Indianapolis region utilized to support transportation planning and traffic analysis efforts.

Feature Layers

  • Current_TAZ_SPE: This layer contains vector polygon geometries defining each Traffic Analysis Zone boundary. Attributes include unique identification codes and geometric measurements such as area and perimeter length. The layer supports the delineation of traffic zones necessary for modeling and visualization of transportation patterns.

Geographic Coverage

The data covers the Indianapolis metropolitan area, providing a critical geographic framework for regional travel demand modeling and transportation planning activities.

Projection: WGS_1984_Web_Mercator_Auxiliary_Sphere

Use Cases

  • Transportation and traffic modeling
  • Urban planning and land use analysis
  • Infrastructure development and policy making
  • Data support for federal and state transportation agencies

results.name: After_Action_Incidents_GCP
results.title: After Action Incident Reports for Highway Traffic Management
results.description:
Overview

This Feature Service provides detailed incident reports for highway traffic management, focusing on after-action analysis of incidents to improve response and recovery strategies. It contains a feature layer documenting comprehensive data related to traffic incidents, including timelines, severity, causes, and impacts on traffic flow.

Feature Layer

  • After_Action_Incidents_GCP: This layer captures a wide range of information about traffic incidents, including crash types and causes, event response status and priority, and time milestones such as detection, verification, response, and clearance times. It integrates contextual information such as weather conditions, event duration, queue lengths, and the presence of emergency resources. 

Geographic Coverage

The dataset covers incidents on Indiana Interstate Routes with further attributes regarding the County of occurrence.

Maintenance: 

This layer is routinely updated by a pipeline that queries relevant data from Google Cloud Platform (GCP). GCP data is updated manually via a one-on-prem Python script that parses a working Excel file maintained by the JTRP.
results.snippet: Comprehensive incident reports with detailed timelines and conditions to support traffic management and after-action reviews in regional highways.

results.title: US Bike Routes
results.description:
In 2015, the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) approved three U.S. Bike Routes (USBR) for a combined 610 miles in Indiana. Recently, in 2021, a fourth USBR was added, connecting Seymour and Indianapolis, bringing the total mileage to 730 miles.

The routes, which are comprised of low traffic roads, bike lanes and trails, are generally designed for experienced, long-distance or touring cyclists to travel through Indiana. However, many sections can accommodate recreational riders and commuters, too.

The routes were a partnership between INDOT, Adventure Cycling Association, Bicycle Indiana, and Hoosier Rail to Trails Council.

• USBR 35: 381 mile north-south route from Lake Michigan to Ohio River

• USBR 36: 58.7 mile east-west route along Lake Michigan

• USBR 50: 160 mile east-west route across central Indiana

• USBR 235: 120 mile between Seymour and Indianapolis
results.snippet: U.S. Bike Routes (USBR) in Indiana.

results.title: Regional Traffic Counts
results.description:
Traffic Counters provide crucial data for transportation planning and engineering studies and a wide variety of other applications and uses.
Each year MACOG collects and analyzes information on traffic traveling in north central Indiana. MACOG collects traffic data at nearly 4,500 locations, on local and state roads, every three-years. There are two kinds of collection methods. The first utilizes road tube to collect a variety of data points about the traffic on a particular segment of road. This would include volume data (how much traffic was there all day and peak hour volume), axle classification (what type of vehicles), speed (how fast each vehicle traveled), and direction (what was the vehicles direction of travel). The other type utilizes video to automatically analyze traffic, particularly at intersections. This would include volume data, vehicle classification, turn movements, and crosswalk data.

results.description:
Boone County, IN Traffic Counts Application.  Map and data created by the Madison County Council of Governments.

The Madison County Council of Governments (MCCOG) has completed Rural Planning Organization Counts (RPO) counts every year in 2010 and 2012 to examine traffic volumes on certain stretches of road.  The count locations are on a three year schedule which allows the county to examine changes in traffic volume over time.  Aside from looking at general volume information within a county, some of the traffic counts also examine the type of vehicle traveling on particular stretches of road.  Classification counts are broken into 13 categories from motorcycles all the way up to double trailer semis.  These counts are extremely useful to illustrate needs for future transportation projects or funding and are also used in the apportion of Federal- Aid Funds for local governments.

results.name: EJScreen_NJ
results.title: EJScreen_NJ
results.description: EJSCREEN is an environmental justice (EJ) screening and mapping tool that provides EPA with a nationally consistent dataset and methodology for calculating "EJ indexes," which can be used for highlighting places that may be candidates for further review, analysis, or outreach as the agency develops programs, policies and other activities. The tool provides both summary and detailed information at the Census block group level or a user-defined area for both demographic and environmental indicators. The summary information is in the form of EJ Indexes which combine demographic information with a single environmental indicator (such as proximity to traffic) that can help identify communities living in areas with greater potential for environmental and health impacts. The tool also provides additional detailed demographic and environmental information to supplement screening analyses. EJSCREEN displays this information in color-coded maps, bar charts, and standard reports. Users should keep in mind that screening tools are subject to substantial uncertainty in their demographic and environmental data, particularly when looking at small geographic areas, such as Census block groups. Data on the full range of environmental impacts and demographic factors in any given location are almost certainly not available directly through this tool, and its initial results should be supplemented with additional information and local knowledge before making any judgments about potential areas of EJ concern. The National-scale Air Toxics Assessment (NATA) environmental indicators and EJ indexes, which include cancer risk, respiratory hazard, neurodevelopment hazard, and diesel particulate matter will be added into EJSCREEN during the first full public update after the soon-to-be-released 2011 dataset is made available. All NATA associated indicator and index elements are currently set to "Null".
results.snippet: Provide a nationally consistent environmental justice screening tool.

results.description:
GaryINsight Land Use Explorer: City of Gary Interactive Zoning, Property, and Development Information Feature Layer

This authoritative GIS feature layer supports the GaryINsight Land Use Explorer and provides centralized access to zoning, parcel, land-use, neighborhood, and development information throughout the City of Gary. It is designed to support municipal planning, zoning administration, development review, property research, community engagement, and public access to geographic information.

The layer may include property location, parcel identification, zoning district, previous zoning classification, existing and future land use, neighborhood, council district, ownership information, development characteristics, and applicable zoning standards. Development information may include permitted-use references, maximum building height, floor area ratio, lot coverage, setbacks, minimum lot area, parking considerations, and overlay-district designations when available.

Residents, property owners, developers, businesses, consultants, and City staff can use the layer to search for properties, identify preliminary zoning classifications, evaluate development patterns, compare zoning with adopted land-use recommendations, and support early project planning. The layer may also be used in web maps, dashboards, ArcGIS Experience Builder applications, zoning reports, neighborhood analyses, and other authorized City planning tools.

Feature geometry and attribute information are compiled from City records, parcel data, adopted zoning actions, planning documents, and related GIS sources. Records are reviewed and updated as new information becomes available. Update dates, validation status, QA/QC status, and data-source fields should be consulted when evaluating individual records.
results.snippet: GaryINsight Land Use Explorer provides access to zoning, land use, and property information across Gary. Users can search by address or parcel number. The interactive map displays zoning districts and related development information. Information is provided for general planning purposes and may be updated. results.name: EmergencyCenter_Clip_Point
results.title: EmergencyCenter_Clip_Point
results.description: Niyam developed this database from the following Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data (HIFLD) Open databases: Local Emergency Operations Centers: HSIP Local Emergency Operations Centers in the United States "The physical location at which the coordination of information and resources to support domestic incident management activities normally takes place. An Emergency Operations Center may be a temporary facility or may be located in a more central or permanently established facility, perhaps at a higher level of organization within a jurisdiction. Emergency Operations Centers may be organized by major functional disciplines (e.g., fire, law enforcement, and medical services), by jurisdiction (e.g., Federal, State, regional, county, city, tribal), or some combination thereof." (Excerpted from the National Incident Management System) The GFI source for this layer contains State and Federal Emergency Operations Centers in addition to local Emergency Operations Centers. This dataset contains these features as well. In cases where an Emergency Operations Center has a mobile unit, TechniGraphics captured the location of the mobile unit as a separate record. This record represents where the mobile unit is stored. If this location could not be verified, a point was placed in the approximate center of the Emergency Operations Centers service area. Effort was made by TechniGraphics to verify whether or not each Emergency Operations Center has a generator on-site and whether or not the Emergency Operations Center is located in a basement. This information is indicated by the values in the [GENERATOR] and [BASEMENT] fields respectively. In cases where more than one record existed for a geographical area (e.g., county, city), TechniGraphics verified whether or not one of the records represented an alternate location. This was indicated by appending "-ALTERNATE" to the value in the [NAME] field. Some Emergency Operations Centers are located at private residences. The [TYPE] field was manually evaluated during the delivery process to compare the records in which the [NAME] field contained "-ALTERNATE". In cases where these values contradicted information that was verified by TechniGraphics (e.g. [NAME] contained "-ALTERNATE" and [TYPE] = "PRIMARY"), the value in the [TYPE] field was changed to match the type indicated by the [NAME] of the verified record. TechniGraphics did not change values in this field if the type was not verified. Records with "-DOD" appended to the end of the [NAME] value are located on a military base, as defined by the Defense Installation Spatial Data Infrastructure (DISDI) military installations and military range boundaries. "#" and "*" characters were automatically removed from standard HSIP fields that TechniGraphics populated. Double spaces were replaced by single spaces in these same fields. At the request of NGA, text fields in this dataset have been set to all upper case to facilitate consistent database engine search results. At the request of NGA, all diacritics (e.g., the German umlaut or the Spanish tilde) have been replaced with their closest equivalent English character to facilitate use with database systems that may not support diacritics. The currentness of this dataset is indicated by the [CONTDATE] field. Based upon this attribute, the oldest record dates from 08/28/2009 and the newest record dates from 11/18/2009. https://hifld-geoplatform.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/local-emergency-operations-center-eoc/about State Emergency Operations Centers: An Emergency Operations Center (EOC) is the physical location at which the coordination of information and resources to support incident management (on-scene operations) activities normally takes place. An EOC may be a temporary facility or may be located in a more central or permanently established facility, perhaps at a higher level of organization within a jurisdiction. EOCs may be organized by major functional disciplines (e.g., fire, law enforcement, medical services), by jurisdiction (e.g., Federal, State, regional, tribal, city, county), or by some combination thereof. The WEBSITE attribute contains a link to Emergency Operations Center or State Emergency Management website. These links contain updated information on emergencies and points of contact. The TRAFFIC attribute contains an link to dynamic traffic information via State 511 Intelligent Traffic System (ITS) website or Department of Transportation (DOT) website. FEMA's Directory Information: https://www.fema.gov/emergency-managers/nims/components/emergency-operations-center Note: The most up to date contact information is found on the State or Territory website. https://hifld-geoplatform.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/state-emergency-operations-centers-eoc Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Regional Headquarters: Regional Headquarters Offices manage, operate and maintain all delegated programs, functions and activities not managed, operated or maintained by headquarters organizational units. The FEMA Regional Offices serve as the primary organizational unit for liaison to states and local governments within each region, and non-governmental and private sector entities within each Regional Office's geographical area. https://hifld-geoplatform.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/federal-emergency-management-agency-fema-regional-offices/about Please refer to the Hazus Inventory Technical Manual for the description of the enhanced methodologies used to estimate building areas and valuations. Please note that due to HIFLD Open data gaps and previous enhancements provided by the Hazus user community, the State Database for HI was not updated using HIFLD Open data. Refer to the Hazus Inventory Manual for information regarding data preparation for the Territories and previous release notes for the HI enhanced data descriptions.
results.snippet: These data are used to estimate the damage (and resulting loss of functionality) associated with emergency operation center facilities for a given flood, hurricane, and/or earthquake scenario. By evaluating this information, the Hazus user can determine whether the emergency response performance of the region is likely to be overwhelmed by the flood, hurricane, earthquake and/or tsunami scenario. Hazus is designed to produce loss estimates for use by state, regional and local governments in planning for earthquake, flood, and wind loss mitigation, emergency preparedness and response and recovery. The damage estimates are used to compute the estimated cost to repair or replace the damaged transportation network of the region.
